intended_object: A specific unsplittable routing in the concrete counterexample instance (a three-commodity single-source network) to the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans-type conjecture: commodity i is sent along its zero-cost s–t_i path. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `cost_clause_alone_satisfiable` and `two_dmax_conclusion_holds_here`.
explanation: The definition is `zeroCostPath`, which sends commodity 0 to [su, uv, vt1], commodity 1 to [su, uv, vw, wt2] and commodity 2 to [su, uv, vw, wt3]. By `arcCost`, every arc on these paths (su, uv, vt1, vw, wt2, wt3) costs 0, so each path really is a zero-cost path. `the_six_are_walks` also checks that each one is an s–t_i walk. This matches the docstring "Route every commodity on its zero-cost path", and the library uses it exactly as that witness: a routing of cost 0 ≤ 58. It is a specific object inside a specific counterexample, so there is no broader setting it should be stated in, and Mathlib has no counterpart.
